scope_depth_novelty.assessment: A compact, coherent decision-support report that compares two subgroup ownership layouts for the current 32-score online-softmax tile, identifies their data and exchange costs, and bounds a fragment-based option. No candidate is timed or adopted.
scope_depth_novelty.novelty: Distinct from R934's broad split-state/key partition and cross-group/global merge survey. R954 assigns rows to existing SIMD16 subgroups after the existing score barrier; it adds no device-wide partial-state phase. Its precision/boundary discussion applies only the retrieved R934 sections 3–4 (lines 45–60); no other R934 body text was read. Distinct from the prior probability experiment, which distributed exp2 work while preserving serial sum order and added two work-group barriers; R954 proposes actual subgroup max/sum reductions. The parallel-pad result combined that earlier path with score pitch 33 and was rejected in favor of pitch 33 alone. The tilepack change leaves softmax ownership unchanged, so its 6-process timing does not isolate this proposal.
scope_depth_novelty.depth: At 1,462 words the report fits the specified budget. The report keeps measured tilepack timing and static ISA counts separate from dynamic utilization, cause, and softmax benefit.

source_contract_review.verified: At that exact SGLang commit, ordinary CUDA forward_extend declines the fused decode/target-verify path, then dispatches no-prefix rows to sparse_gqa_fwd_interface_triton and prefix rows to pack_qsa_prefill_kv(output_dtype=q.dtype) plus sparse_gqa_fwd_interface_triton_ck. The pinned sparse_attn.py source scales Q by scale and log2(e) before converting back to Q dtype, initializes max/normalizer/value accumulator in FP32, masks invalid selected entries in scores, performs tl.max/tl.sum along the selected-token axis, casts P to V dtype for PV, and allocates output like Q. The prefix kernel casts packed K/V to Q dtype. In the configured BF16 case these source expressions support BF16 Q/K/V/P/output storage with FP32 online state/accumulation. The Strata 32-cell block is a different tile boundary; SGLang's BLOCK_N is selected by query count.
source_contract_review.model_integration: The pinned Qwen4-Exp model layer marks QSA from its config, builds its indexer, and passes topk_indices through self.attn; its QSA helper resolves backend-owned indexer metadata. This statically connects the model family's QSA layer to the sparse attention interface, while the concrete get_attn_backend instance remains runner/configuration-dependent.
source_contract_review.applicability_limit: This is a source-level contract for the ordinary non-CP, non-speculative CUDA extend branch, conditional on the runner resolving QwenSparseAttnBackend. forward_extend also has context-parallel, speculative, CPU, and device/config-dependent paths. Neither the R954 report nor this read-only review ran SGLang or proves which branch/dtypes a particular model runtime selected. Triton tl.max/tl.sum establish logical reductions, not exact lane mapping, lowering, FMA behavior, or performance. SGLang has no explicit all-missing-row guard in these kernels; Strata's guarded zero-row and nonfinite behavior remains an additional local requirement.

api_and_fragment_review.sycl: Khronos SYCL 2020 revision 12 defines group functions as convergent: every work-item must call the same function under the same conditions. permute_group_by_xor requires the same mask across the subgroup and returns the XOR-selected lane value. The proposed Candidate A and B layouts respect those static constraints if validity remains data and every lane takes every reduction/exchange, including padded rows.
api_and_fragment_review.intel_matrix: Pinned Intel/LLVM oneAPI matrix documentation at cf12c3783cc6a7adaf76e54c6a4f11f81ec8599b lists BMG BF16 matrix combinations and says the runtime matrix_combinations query is authoritative. Its BMG load/store requirements include 4-byte pointer alignment and byte stride divisible by 8. The pinned Intel matrix extension at a13d57a7f99adac86be159be55030e4cead7fd25 defines coordinate-aware joint_matrix_apply and ext_intel_packed/VNNI layout. Current Strata source maps score fragments as subgroup 0/1 for rows 0–7 and cell halves 0–15/16–31, subgroup 2/3 for rows 8–15 and the same halves. Thus each row's halves are produced by distinct subgroups; a direct fragment-local 32-cell reduction is not available without communication or retile. The documented coordinate callback does not define physical lane-to-fragment ownership or, by itself, prove race-free complete-row reduction. R954 correctly avoids assuming undocumented lane mapping and keeps direct fragment reduction conditional.
api_and_fragment_review.collective_cost_correction: No additional work-group barrier/global scratch/launch is a valid design target, but reduce_over_group and permute_group_by_xor are still subgroup group functions with synchronization/exchange cost. Read 'no barrier' as no added work-group barrier; do not infer zero synchronization cost.

corrections.detail: The report cites both prefill kernel bodies but not their higher-level resolver. Review verified the pinned Qwen4-Exp/QSA model integration and forward_extend resolver. The no-prefix/prefix calls apply only when the runner resolves QwenSparseAttnBackend and takes ordinary non-CP, non-speculative CUDA extend; CPU, CP, speculative and other paths remain separate. Keep BF16 conditional on actual q/k/v dtype and pack configuration. The source is not runtime proof.

The Intel coordinate-aware joint_matrix_apply example establishes element coordinates and shows an accumulator expression; it does not specify lane ownership, storage scope, race freedom, or a complete subgroup row reduction. R954's cross-subgroup-half conclusion is independently supported by the pinned Strata dispatch and remains valid.

One short line of Intel API specification example code is reproduced in the report. Its pinned Apache-2.0-with-LLVM-exceptions source is attributed and checked; distinguish this small documentation excerpt from copying/adapting any engine code, helper, test, or diagnostic.

The candidates avoid an added work-group barrier/global scratch/launch. Their SYCL subgroup collectives still synchronize or exchange within the subgroup and have costs; the report identifies reduction/exchange stages, but this distinction should be preserved in retrieval.
